per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

acceptance: the engine exports a subtree walk that answers each entry below a tag with its depth, in the sibling order the caller's comparator gives, and a goal predicate read off `kind` and `parent`; `descendantsOf` is one call of that walk, `harness/goals.ts` holds no walk and no predicate of its own, and `src/queueGoals.ts` and `harness/gates.ts` read the exported predicate — with the goals block, the served order and the goal-rank gate unchanged in what they print and refuse

interface.changes: the engine exports a subtree walk answering each entry below a tag with its depth, in the sibling order a caller's comparator gives, and the root-group predicate it already decides internally; `descendantsOf` stays, as one call of that walk
interface.hides: the children map, the visited set and the sibling sort each caller was building for itself — a consumer that wants a subtree in an order no longer rebuilds the descent to get one
interface.rejected: leaving the package its own depth walk and exporting nothing — two descents over one forest answer differently the first time either grows a leg, which is the shape the ruling turned down

notes: Operator ruling, inbox 2026-10-07: engine walks, caller orders. Collides with the standing `src/PendingSchema.ts` and `harness/gates.ts` entries by design.
